ruling.reasoning:
The trace settles the route element: no off-route segment was measured (RD-1 ✗), and the GPS record shows 8.5 km actual against 8.5 km optimal, +0.0 km (-0%) [F1]; the fare record agrees that billed distance 8.5 km does not exceed the optimal route [F3]. With no unexempted segment there is nothing for RD-2 to refund, so segment_findings is empty and the distance component of $11.99 contains no excess mileage [F5][RD-1].

The rider's stated grievance — "the fare was higher than I expected … heavy rain, the driver must have taken a longer route" — is answered by the records rather than by the driver's word: the trip ran 22.0 min against a 16.3 min estimate (+5.7 min) [F2], and on this RydeTAXI metered fare that elapsed time was billed as a $5.72 time component on 22.0 min [F5]. RD-2 only refunds unexempted extra mileage, and there is none, so the meter accrual stands [F3][RD-2].

No refund formula is engaged: the trip is a metered RydeTAXI fare (base $3.90 + distance $11.99 (8.50 km) + time $5.72 (22.0 min) + waiting $0.00 + platform $1.47 = $23.08) [F5] at surge 1.0× with no discount [F4]. Nothing in the itemisation is unpublished or unsupported, so FARE-1 yields no refund line [F5][FARE-1].

The slowness that generated the time charge is corroborated externally and needs no exemption finding: PIE and Airport Boulevard were both at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) across 17:09–17:47, covering the 17:20–17:42 window [F8][F9], in heavy rain of 18.5 mm [F11], with no traffic incident recorded near the route [F10]. Band 3 is neither RD-4(a) (no incident) nor RD-4(b) (band 1 or 2 only, and only as corroboration), so no segment is exempted on that ground — but no deviation exists to exempt, so the point does not change the outcome [F10][RD-4].

No consent question arises: there are no in-app chat messages at all [F6], so no rider message agreed to any route or stop, and the driver's post-trip statement that he followed the app route [F7] is a statement, not consent; it merely aligns with the system records [F1][F6][F7][RD-5]. No profile fact decides anything here: the driver's 1 dispute / 0 upheld in 90 days [F13] does not meet RD-6's "repeated" basis, and the rider's clean record [F12] is irrelevant to the outcome [F13][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the driver's statement and the (empty) chat — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears; the complaint is a fare/route expectation issue and the driver's statement is explanatory [F6][F7]. Safety_concern is therefore "none" [F6][F7][SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the GPS distance comparison, the fare itemisation and the timeline of duration are all present and consistent, so no record needed for this ruling is missing [F1][F3][F5][F2].

rejected_claims.reason: Partly rejected as to its RD-4 framing: the traffic records [F8][F9] are band 3 and [F10] shows no incident, so neither RD-4(a) nor RD-4(b) exempts anything; the conditions explain duration only and the ruling rests on the absence of any off-route segment [F1][F3] under RD-1/RD-2, not on an RD-4 exemption.

Rejected as an exemption argument: [F8][F9] place the route at band 3 (20–29 km/h) and [F10] records no incident, so RD-4's formal exemptions are not satisfied; the driver's compliant outcome follows from [F1][F3] (8.5 km = 8.5 km optimal) and the metered time component [F5], not from RD-4.

Accepted in result but rejected in part as to SAFE-1/SAFE-2: [F6][F7] contain no threat or dangerous-driving allegation, so my safety finding is 'none' rather than an escalation; the account-flag point is correct — [F13] shows 0 upheld, so RD-6 does not apply.
